US Open hub — UX-P139, your twelve items. SHIPPED components, the app's own compiled CSS, a 390px viewport, and the ROUTE'S OWN OUTPUT over register v7. Each phone scrolls.
  1. Item 6 — the chart has an x-axis. Three dated ticks (first, middle, last) and “29d shown” beside the count. The y-axis has always been a labelled fixed 0–100; the x had nothing, so a falling line could be a day or a month. Labels are HTML, not SVG text, because the plot is non-uniformly scaled and text inside it stretches.
  2. Item 9 — decided matches print a real score. 76 of them, from ESPN's tennis scoreboard: per-set line scores, winner first, joined on the registered player pair. The UX-P138 artifact's scores were hand-written because nothing here held a tennis result. That is fixed — see the “Finished” section in every panel.
  3. Item 10 — the questions section was invisible, and now is not. It rendered in all nine of the last artifact's panels; it rendered its EMPTY state as a dashed 12.5px box between two solid white cards, which reads as a divider. Same border, same background, same weight as a populated card now, and it names what will be there. The demo state carries a yellow DEMO banner (last panel) so it can never be mistaken for production.
  4. Item 11 — the sentence you could not parse. It meant: “Can Alcaraz win a second major this year?” and “Can Sinner win a second major this year?” are one question with a different name in it, so showing both is a template. The runtime rule dropped one of them at every render, which hid the repetition instead of removing it. Register v7 drops Alcaraz's from the file (Sinner's 55.5% is the closer question, and his participation is the one in doubt), so there is no template left to cap.
  5. Item 12 — doubles is built and empty. Five draws in the register vocabulary, five in the results component. Censused 2026-08-26: zero US Open doubles markets at either source, so nothing renders. ESPN already carries all three doubles draws' RESULTS (63/63/21 competitions), so the results half lights up the day anyone asks.
  6. Item 7 — matches do NOT click through, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. Checked 2026-08-26: none of the registered matchups has an events row, so there is no page to open. The link is wired, register-owned, and dark. The honest assessment of the destination is in the report and it is worse news than the missing link.
Boards: real production read, 80 contenders, and #2199 is fixed — both boards read live at ~2.5h, where every prior artifact had them 8–34 days dark. Matches: 113 on the card, 0 inside the live window. Finished: 76 with scores. Questions: two curated, both dark, so the section is empty and says which.
ON THE 15-DAY-OLD DATA THAT SPOOKED YOU (item 2): it was real, not a mock artifact — and the boards half is already fixed. The outright fields were genuinely 8–34 days dark (#2199); this artifact is the first one where they are not. The reach ladder behind the bracket grid was genuinely 27 hours stale at capture. The cause was structural, not a bug: Gamma caps offset pagination at 2,000, so the scanning poll rotates a window and reaches a given event roughly once a day. This queue ships a 10-minute task that asks Gamma for exactly the market IDs the register pins — a read that does not paginate and so is not capped.

The production guarantee is not that data is never old. It is that old data can never look current, and it is enforced in three places rather than promised: the server sets probability_is_live and a client cannot round past it; a row is as fresh as its OLDEST contributing leg, never its newest; and an absent timestamp reads as dark, not as fresh. The treatment is visible on this page — every muted number carries its own age in words, and a number old enough to stop being a price is removed rather than shown quietly.
